description: The north wall of the two-storey, hip-roofed main (west) block only, the sheet's right-hand block: from its north-east corner board (sheet left, where the lower-roofed two-storey dining block, set back 8'-11", begins and a downspout runs down) to its north-west (front) corner board at the sheet's right end, from grade to the top of the box gutter/cornice; one window per storey, the lower one with a crown cap.

length.note: first floor plan's top string over the parlor's north wall, 6'-11" + 2'-5" + 6'-11" = 16'-3" (the house truth's first chain leg); the elevation scales 16.19 ft between the corner boards' outer edges (x 7646 to 10075 px at 150 px/ft); the second floor plan gives 16'-1"

eave.note: mean of pass A (19.79) and pass B (19.82). A: the house's eave (west elevation, grade to the top of the box gutter/cornice), the same cornice on this block. This sheet's right string prints 1'-1" + 9'-2" + 10'-6" (= 20'-9") but its ticks scale 1.10 + 9.20 + 9.52 = 19.82 ft (grade tick y 6831.5, eave tick y 3858.5 px), so 10'-6" reads as a misprint for 9'-6". The drawn grade slopes along this wall (y 6879.5 px at the sheet-left corner, 6844 px at the right; mean 6861.8), which puts the cornice top 20.02 ft above the mean drawn grade. | B: the north elevation's right height string prints grade to first floor 1'-1", first to second floor 9'-2", second floor to eave 10'-6" (a misprint: its ticks are 1429.5 px = 9.53 ft apart; read as 9'-6" the string gives 19'-9"). Scaled between the string's grade tick (6831) and eave tick (3858): 19.82 ft, which agrees with the house truth's eave (19'-9 1/2" printed on the west elevation, top of the box gutter/cornice). The drawn ground is at 6880 at the left corner and 6845 at the right corner; sill_ft uses the string's grade tick, 6831.

openings.note: mean of the passes. A: top is the top of the crown cap (the cap overhangs the casings to x 8615 and 9130 px; the width is the casings'); bottom is the sill's bottom | B: double-hung with a cornice head: top at the cap's crown (5429; the cap projects about 0.2 ft past the casings, not counted); bottom at the sill's bottom (6437), the sill band running 6409-6437 between the casings

mean of the passes. A: top is the frame's top line between the two cornice brackets that sit over the side casings (brackets and their base blocks run from the frieze at y 3990 down to y 4150 px; not counted: counted as trim they would raise the top by about 0.7 ft) | B: double-hung; its head is directly under the cornice's frieze, with cornice brackets over its casings (left out)

porch: Nothing stands in front of this wall; the open front porch is beyond its sheet-right (west) corner and the dining block is set back at its sheet-left end.

photos.which: the tall two-storey wall at the right of the picture (one window on each floor), not the lower parts at the left
the wall at the left of the picture: the two-storey end wall with one window on each floor

note: Two independent readings of the elevation merged by work/merge_facades.py.
